inspection_outcome: Six established findings: two Major and four Minor, with explicit counterevidence and bounded repair scope.
summary: The local obstruction depends on choices, and the fixed degree20 realization theorem has an exact counterexample. Further local quantifier, signature-characterization, dimension and root-hypothesis defects are proved.

problems.title: Local residue exchanges are misclassified and epsilon is not choice independent
problems.source_location: PDF p19 Notation7.2; pp21–22 Proposition8.1, Lemma8.3 and epsilon^p definition; pp25,29 Theorems9.7,12.1
problems.claim: Every admissible local datum gives the same epsilon pairing on C0(I).
problems.assumptions: F=f^2(X+1)^4, f=X^2−7X+1; signature(4,4), block signatures(2,2), D−=81 squareclass1; C0,C1 and delta=0 all hold.
problems.check_method: Exact local trace forms, determinants, Hilbert symbols and equivariant residues, independently reconstructed by root.
problems.decisive_evidence: E=Q(sqrt5) ramifies only at5 and f mod5=(X−1)^2, so the printed Pi_{f,X+1} is empty. At3 alpha=(7+3sqrt5)/2 reduces to−1. With b_lambda=<2lambda,−10lambda>, rows (b1+b1,<1,1,1,1>) and (b3+b1,<3,3,1,1>) have ambientH^4 and total residue0. Their Hasse coordinates are(0,0),(1,1), but c(f)=1,c(X+1)=0 is permitted, giving epsilon0 and1. A separate quartic example h=X4+3X3+10X2+3X+1 shows a false positive edge; details in TeX.
problems.result: The choice-independence assertion is false within the numerical and delta=0 range used downstream.
problems.counterevidence: The main quadratic input has an actual global hyperbolic realization diag(A,A^{-t}) plus−id onH². This is not a no-realization example, and not a counterexample to every Salem theorem.
problems.impact: The prescribed obstruction is not well-defined as printed; its use in the main arithmetic criterion requires substantial repair.

correction.statement: Define exchanges from actual local residue images, including unramified nonsplit blocks reducing to±1, and reprove orbit/choice independence and global sufficiency.
correction.verification: Both explicit failures verified. A complete replacement obstruction theorem has not been proved.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Notation7.2 p19 defines the linear-factor edges using ramified places; Proposition8.1 and Lemma8.3 pp21-22 assert orbit and choice independence for the local sets of Sections5-6. Their obstruction enters Theorems9.7 and12.1.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Take f=X?-7X+1,F=f?(X+1)^4, signatures(2,2) on each factor and total(4,4). F(0)=1,F(1)=400,F(-1)=0; the stated numerical conditions hold and D_-=81 has squareclass1. Q(sqrt5) ramifies only at5, where f reduces to(X-1)?, so the printed Pi_(f,X+1) is empty and c=(1,0) is allowed. At3 alpha=(7+3sqrt5)/2 reduces to-1. The trace form b_lambda is<2lambda,-10lambda>. Compare rows A:(b1+b1;<1,1,1,1>) and B:(b3+b1;<3,3,1,1>). Each block determinant has squareclass1; both block Hasse invariants change by1 in rowB, so the total spaces are the same eight-dimensional hyperbolic space. The odd-valuation equivariant residues in rowB are<-1,-1> and<1,1> in the same chi_- summand and cancel; both rows therefore have delta0 and belong to the same C0^3. Relative to the actual reference forms, a=(0,0),a'=(1,1), giving epsilon_a(c)=0 and epsilon_a'(c)=1. Primary independently checked the Hilbert-symbol, residue, determinant and signature conditions against the actual definitions.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The secondary quartic h=X4+3X3+10X2+3X+1 also shows the reverse false-edge direction: at3 its only ramified nonsplit block reduces to-1 while the printed condition adds an edge to+1. This is corroboration, not a substitute for the full-assumption primary example. The primary F nevertheless has a global integral realization diag(A,A^-transpose) on a hyperbolic rank4 block, plus -1 on H?. Thus the established Major defect is the core obstruction's choice independence, not nonexistence for F or a refutation of every Salem realization result.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Classify actual residue exchanges, including unramified nonsplit blocks reducing to a linear character, then re-prove stability, orbits, choice independence and the affected global obstruction criterion.

problems.title: Claim2 allows an impossible determinant in a single linear eigenspace
problems.claim: Arbitrary units u+,u− with product(−1)^n can prescribe the extant component determinant.
problems.check_method: Direct Gram determinant modulo4 and comparison with 2-adic squareclasses.
problems.decisive_evidence: Even unimodular rank2 Gram[[2a,b],[b,2c]] requires b odd; determinant≡3mod4, impossible squareclass1. The same F gives valuation sum0, contradicting p11's asserted odd sum. The p9 single-component determinant exponent n1 also fails in this example.
problems.result: The printed universal single-component determinant claim is false.
problems.counterevidence: H with identity realizes F. Proposition11.1 asks prescribed determinants only when both linear eigenspaces are present.
problems.impact: Local proof needs a narrower quantifier and corrected determinant choice; the ordinary existence theorem is not disproved by this example.

correction.statement: Remove arbitrary determinant prescription for a sole linear eigenspace and choose total determinant consistently, using n where required; delete false parity inference.
correction.verification: Rank2 counterexample and hyperbolic replacement checked. Full referenced 2-adic existence proof not rederived.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Claim2 p9 permits arbitrary units u_plus,u_minus with product(-1)^n even when only one linear eigenspace exists; the proof explicitly includes that single-eigenspace case.

Its Gram matrix[[2a,b],[b,2c]] has b odd and determinant4ac-b? congruent3 mod4, whereas a unit in squareclass1 is1 mod8. Contradiction. Here both valuations of F1 at ?1 are0, also contradicting the p11 oddness assertion.

Proposition11.1 p28 requires both linear eigenspaces before prescribing both determinants, and is not refuted by this single-eigenspace example.

problems.title: Signature-map characterization misses joint uniqueness and nonreal reciprocal blocks
problems.source_location: PDF p13 Proposition3.7 and p14 construction
problems.claim: Conditions(a)–(e) characterize all semisimple real signature maps.
problems.assumptions: General real semisimple isometries, not only Salem-plus-cyclotomic spectra.
problems.check_method: Identity-map multiplicities and a four-dimensional off-unit-circle reciprocal-pair counterexample.
problems.decisive_evidence: For positive identity onR4, both (X−1)^4 and (X−1)^2(X+1)^2 satisfy(a) alone. Separately P=(X²+4)(X²+1/4), tau(u)=(3,1) ifP dividesu and0 otherwise satisfies the printed nonzero-polynomial conditions, but any corresponding isometry would have two totally isotropic 2D primary spaces and signature(2,2).
problems.result: Literal uniqueness and general sufficiency fail.
problems.counterevidence: Joint multiplicity condition(d) resolves identity example; Salem-plus-cyclotomic spectra have no nonreal off-circle quartets.
problems.impact: General classification requires corrected conditions; practical Salem applications are not directly refuted by the quartet.

correction.statement: State uniqueness after all multiplicity conditions; require balanced hyperbolic multiplicities for all non-self-reciprocal factors; define zero-polynomial convention.
correction.verification: Counterexamples checked and mathematical need for hyperbolic blocks proved; full rewritten classification not certified.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Proposition3.7 p13 claims uniqueness in(a) alone and sufficient signature conditions(a)-(e) for all real symmetric factors. The printed definition of rad(0) has no supplied meaning.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For identity on positive R4, both(X-1)^4 and(X-1)?(X+1)? satisfy the stated(a) selection conditions; the joint multiplicity condition(d), not(a) alone, selects the characteristic polynomial. For the separate sufficiency defect put P=(X?+4)(X?+1/4) and tau(u)=(3,1) when P divides u and0 otherwise. On nonzero polynomials the printed algebraic conditions hold: a symmetric polynomial cannot contain just one member of this reciprocal quadratic pair; radical and coprime additivity preserve the assignment; all symmetric irreducibles and real reciprocal linear pairs in(d)-(e) have value and required multiplicity0. A semisimple isometry with this P instead has two two-dimensional totally isotropic primary spaces, forcing signature(2,2). The argument persists under the natural value at the zero polynomial, but does not pretend that the source actually defined rad(0).
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: The Salem-cyclotomic applications have no off-circle nonreal quartets. The finding is a bounded failure of an abstract characterization and its domain/uniqueness wording, not a demonstrated failure of those applications.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Place uniqueness after the joint multiplicity conditions, add the hyperbolic constraint for every non-self-reciprocal factor pair, and specify the zero-polynomial convention.

problems.decisive_evidence: The trace polynomial Y²−Y−3 has one root>2 and another in(−2,2), and discriminant norm−3 is nonsquare. Phi29 has degree28, so delta cannot occur in a rank22 integral H² representation.

problems.title: Theorem24.1(a) fails for its specified degree20 characteristic polynomial
problems.source_location: PDF p51 fixed F=S(X²−1), Theorem24.1(a); p52 final by-construction positivity assertion; p35 type(P)
problems.claim: Odd, square-free coprime endpoint values suffice for a realizable isometry with the fixed F and Salem signature.
problems.assumptions: S=X20+X19−sum_{j=3}^{17}X^j+X+1; S(1)=−11,S(−1)=1. Both meet the endpoint hypotheses.
problems.check_method: Root's independent exact BigInt modular irreducibility and rational interval checks; primitive-lattice projection, discriminant index and binary-lattice classification.
problems.decisive_evidence: S mod2 irreducible by x^(2^20)=x and gcds at exponents10,4 equal1; ten strict rational sign intervals prove the Salem root pattern. If the fixed realization exists, N=cyclotomic rank2 has det dividing11, hence11. Its unique positive form[[2,1],[1,6]] has roots±e1. Type(P) forces matrix[[1,1],[0,−1]], acting−1 onA_N=Z/11. But S(t)N*subsetN and S(t)=−5−6t force t=+1 onA_N, contradiction.
problems.result: No isometry with the specified polynomial and Salem signature can satisfy type(P) for this S.
problems.counterevidence: Changing the cyclotomic factor can avoid the contradiction. The example does not disprove general degree20 Salem realizability or the broader result attributed to Takada.
problems.impact: A theorem statement with fixed characteristic polynomial is false; its final positivity inference needs substantive correction.

correction.statement: Restrict the fixed-polynomial assertion or add discriminant/chamber compatibility; alternatively allow the cyclotomic factor to change.
correction.verification: Full counterexample and exact Salem certificate established; no classification of all corrected endpoint conditions proved.

acceptance_check.source_claim_and_assumptions: Theorem24.1(a) pp51-52 fixes F=S(X?-1) and the exact signature map tau_delta, and asserts a realizable isometry. Definitions15.4-15.5 p35 require its cyclotomic restriction to preserve a root chamber.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Use S=X20+X19-sum_(j=3)^17 Xj+X+1. S(1)=-11,S(-1)=1 meet the odd square-free coprime hypotheses. The retained exact computation and the separately implemented current native integer/Fraction computation verify the trace identity, ten disjoint strict sign-change intervals (nine in(-2,2),one above2), and the full mod2 irreducibility criterion: X^(2^20)=X and both gcds for exponents2^10 and2^4 equal1. Hence S is a genuine degree20 Salem polynomial. If the claimed t existed, its primitive negative rank2 cyclotomic lattice N has S(t)N* contained in N by projection from unimodular L. Thus |det N| divides11 and cannot equal1, so equals11. Reduction of positive even binary forms makes N(-1) uniquely[[2,1],[1,6]], with roots?e1. Type(P) forces t(e1)=e1; characteristic X?-1 then forces t=[[1,1],[0,-1]], acting by-1 on the discriminant generator(-e1+2e2)/11. But S(t)=-5-6t must vanish on that group and forces t=+1 mod11. This contradiction refutes the fixed-polynomial assertion, not merely an unproved sentence in its proof.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_core_dependency: Integral root reflections extend to the ambient unimodular lattice and act trivially on the rational Salem part. A Weyl correction can preserve a chamber while changing the cyclotomic polynomial, so the broader degree20 Salem realization conclusion is not disproved by this fixed-F counterexample. The actual core fixed-polynomial theorem remains Major even though a broader formulation may survive.
acceptance_check.repair_scope: Restrict the fixed-polynomial assertion by the required discriminant/chamber compatibility, or allow an explicitly justified change of cyclotomic polynomial. A complete corrected global realization theorem is not certified.

clarifications: Weyl root reflections give an integral chamber correction when cyclotomic factors may change; equal Witt residues alone do not identify a fixed gluing.
The simple Salem eigenline supports Proposition25.5, so a generic missing-Kahler-cone objection to surface identification is rejected.
